label: token right after a digit 2 at position 1 or 2 of the original sequence
explanation: Fires on the original-phase step right after the digit 2 was input, but only when that 2 sat at position 0 or 1 (so the active step is t=1 or t=2). It does not depend on the current input token. Magnitude depends on position: when 2 is the first token (active at t=1) the activation is near max (~0.97-1.0 of max, 62% of the mass). When 2 is at position 1 (active at t=2) it is weaker (~0.5-0.66). A 2 at position 2 gives only tiny activations (<0.1) at t=3, and later positions give nothing. Silent at t=0, on the delimiter, and in the copy phase (23 negligible activations), and silent after any token other than 2. Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.989, F1 0.994, mass recall 0.999.

issues: The claims hold. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.989, F1 0.994, mass recall 0.9993, correlation 0.97. Zero false positives on test.

Profile matches the explanation. No activity at t=0 or on the delimiter. Only 23 copy-phase activations, with negligible mass. Mass share is 0.623 at t=1 and 0.377 at t=2. t=3 has 359 activations with 0.1% of the mass. Activation is flat across in_tok (lift about 1.1 for every token), so it does not depend on the current input.

Test misses (378, 0.1% of mass) are all faint activations at t=3 after a 2 at position 2 (0.01-0.13), as the explanation says. Adding t=3 to the predicate raises n_predicted from 33k to 50k, which would badly hurt precision. Excluding t=3 is correct, so no better predicate is needed.

Minor wording issue: the label says '2 at position 1 or 2', but the explanation and predicate mean the 2 is at 0-indexed position 0 or 1, so the active step is t=1 or 2. The label should say the active step is t=1 or 2, or that the 2 is at position 0 or 1 (0-indexed).
skeptic.revised_label: step right after a digit 2 in the first or second original position (active at t=1 or t=2)

final_label: step right after a digit 2 in the first or second original position (active at t=1 or t=2)
